entries.text: The Wausau City Council returned from closed session on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, to vote on settling contamination claims tied to city water wells. The council approved the settlements 10-0 and authorized Mayor Doug Diny to sign the necessary documents. An alderperson reminded the public about a December 2 Committee of the Whole meeting on retaining young people in Wausau. The meeting then adjourned.

The Weston Parks Committee met on Monday, November 23, 2026 and voted to set the concession stand as the next fundraising goal for Kennedy Park's Friends group. The committee reviewed end-of-season survey results from the Kennedy Park farmers market, finding mostly positive feedback with parking and traffic flow as the top complaints.

The DC Everest School Board met on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, and approved several policy readings, a budget calendar, and new course proposals. Board member Larry Schaefer raised concerns about a student grade eligibility rule in Policy 2430, arguing students with an F grade should not be allowed to compete in extracurriculars. The board then approved the policy anyway on a voice vote.
The Police & Fire Commission is scheduled to interview two candidates for Deputy Chief with the Wausau Police Department in a closed session on December 2.

items.item: Interview candidates for Wausau Police Department Deputy Chief

entries.text: The Wausau Transit Commission met on November 19, 2026, and unanimously approved four action items: issuing an RFP for new cash-only fare boxes, authorizing bids for replacement of exterior doors at the Metro Ride facility, authorizing bids for ceiling replacement at the facility, and aligning Metro Ride's procurement policy with the City of Wausau's.

The Marathon County Board held a special meeting that included a closed session, after which supervisors voted unanimously to refer to the executive committee the formation of a response to Aligning Energy, development of a legal strategy, and to solicit input from Farmland First and Wisconsinites for Local Control.

The Village of Kronenwetter's Administrative Policy Committee held its November 17, 2026 meeting, approving several budget-related recommendations including a $5,000 park grant match, a multi-item 2026 budget amendment, and health insurance renewals for two employee groups.
The Wausau Board of Public Works held a brief meeting in which two claims were acted upon: one approved and one denied. The meeting concluded quickly with no extended discussion or public comment.

The Wausau Plan Commission held its November 17, 2026 meeting, addressing a contested rezoning request for 317 East Kent Street and reviewing the housing chapter of the city's updated comprehensive plan. The rezoning request from urban mixed-use to heavy industrial failed on a 2-2 tie vote and will advance to the full City Council for a decision at its December 8 meeting.

contested.item: Rezoning of 317 East Kent Street from Urban Mixed-Use to Heavy Industrial

entries.text: The Wausau Board of Public Works met on November 17th and handled three items: approving prior meeting minutes, opening 15 bids for the 2026 demolition of the former MBX South building at 207 North 1st Avenue (with no award made pending funding confirmation), and approving a contractor pay estimate before moving into closed session.

The Marathon County Board held a special meeting focused on the Hub City Wind Project's proposed Joint Development Agreement (JDA) from Alliant Energy and a separate issue involving Bug Tussle's failure to make required bond payments.

The Village of Weston Finance and HR Committee met on November 16 and took action on accounts receivable write-offs and 2026 budget amendments, both of which were approved unanimously for forwarding to the village board. The committee deadlocked 3-3 on a motion to recommend Option G for sanitary sewer rate increases, with the item deferred to the December 21 meeting for updated financial figures.

contested.item: Recommend village proceed with Option G for 2027 sanitary sewer rates

entries.text: The Kronenwetter Village Plan Commission held its November 16, 2026 meeting, approving recommendations on a septic tank ordinance amendment, the Green Tree Trails subdivision final plat, and a stormwater maintenance agreement for the County Road XX distribution center.

The Village of Weston Board of Trustees held its regular meeting on Monday, November 16, 2026, highlighted by a contentious 4-3 vote to adopt the 2027 operating budget and an equally divided 4-3 vote on the debt service and capital funds budgets, with the three newer trustees (Beck, Clark, and Olson) voting against both over concerns about excessive borrowing and spending of TIF district closure funds.

No major votes were taken; the meeting concluded with a motion to adjourn and a note that an additional county board meeting is scheduled for November 17th at 6:00 p.m.

The Marathon County Board Executive Committee held a wide-ranging meeting covering the Bugtussle bond default crisis, the Hub City Wind Farm joint development agreement, a county road funding policy, and strategic plan updates.

entries.text: The Marathon County Public Safety Committee held its November 2026 meeting focused heavily on the Sheriff's Office's Flock automatic license plate reader (ALPR) program, with significant public input and committee debate over data privacy, oversight, and whether to defund the cameras. The committee also received presentations on the Sheriff's Office drone program and a 2027 budget overview.

The Wausau Board of Public Works held a brief meeting in which members approved a list of contractors for city work. The meeting was extremely short, consisting of a single contractor approval vote followed by adjournment.

The Village of Kronenwetter Board held its November 9, 2026 meeting primarily to adopt the 2027 operating budget, including all three budget resolutions covering the general fund, all other funds, and the capital improvements program. The board also formally appointed Connie Nowak as village clerk and renewed its legal services agreement with Wolfram, Gamoke and Hutchinson.

The Village of Weston Public Works Committee held its regular meeting on November 10, 2026, covering a detailed infiltration and inflow (I&I) study presentation for the Rothschild sewer basin, a sewer rate increase recommendation, and approvals of several intergovernmental agreements and design contracts.

entries.meeting: Human Resources, Finance & Property Committee Meeting
entries.text: The Marathon County Human Resources, Finance & Property Committee held a brief meeting focused on authorizing publication of the proposed 2027 county budget. The committee unanimously approved publication of the budget notice, which includes a proposed tax levy of $66,248,545 and a mill rate of 3.4773, advancing the budget process toward a public hearing on November 2nd and final county board action on November 10th.

The Wausau Human Resources Committee met on October 12th and took action on two items: approving a request for an additional HR staff member (to be incorporated into the 2027 budget rather than a budget modification), and voting to maintain the existing summer hours schedule and traditional full-week winter hours rather than adopting year-round summer hours.

entries.text: The Wausau Infrastructure and Facilities Committee met on Thursday, October 8, 2026, and took action on several significant items, most notably voting to amend the city's Department of Public Works winter maintenance policy to permit snowplow counterflow to traffic on center median boulevard streets, a change sought by residents of Highland Park and the southeast side for three years.
